name: Megeve
description: Megeve was built in the 1920s as a winter playground for European aristocracy — the Rothschild family created it as an alternative to St Moritz. It has genuine old-town charm, cobbled streets, a central square with a 12th-century church, horse-drawn carriages, and some of the best dining in the Alps (including Flocons de Sel — 3 Michelin stars). The skiing is across two mountain sectors (Rochebrune and Mont d'Arbois) linked with Saint-Gervais for 325km total. Golf course in summer.

overview.atmosphere: The French Riviera of the Alps. Refined, historic, built by the Rothschilds in the 1920s. Elegant chalet architecture, Michelin-starred dining, luxury boutiques.

beyond_skiing.ice_skating: Outdoor rink under the stars + Palais Megève 1,800 m² Olympic rink. Curling, eisstock, broom ball
beyond_skiing.non_ski_activities: 50+ non-ski activities listed by tourist office. Paragliding, snowshoeing, dog sledding, helicopter tours, swimming, climbing, cinema, market

food_and_drink.best_restaurants: Le Saint Germain (traditional French), Le Prieure (river terrace), Les Enfants Terribles (playful, good value)

apres_and_nightlife.nightlife_clubbing: Le Xenius (lively), La Folie Douce Megeve (seasonal)
apres_and_nightlife.quiet_evenings: Sophisticated, elegant, less rowdy than Val Thorens. Champagne crowd rather than beer crowd.

villages.name: Megeve Centre
villages.character: Historic old town, cobbled streets, 12th-century church, luxury boutiques, Michelin dining, horse-drawn carriages. The anti-purpose-built resort.

villages.name: Le Mont d'Arbois
villages.character: Higher satellite, quieter, closer to slopes

honest_drawbacks: Low altitude (1,113m) — snow reliability is a concern early/late season
Expensive — one of the priciest resorts
